title: A risk prediction model for neovascular glaucoma secondary to proliferative diabetic retinopathy based on Boruta feature selection and random forest
summary: A random-forest model predicted neovascular glaucoma risk in diabetic-retinopathy patients with reported diagnostic metrics. The result is limited to the reported study population and evaluation; the source does not establish transfer to other populations or improved clinical outcomes.
organization: The Second Clinical Medical College of Jinan University, Shenzhen Eye Hospital, Shenzhen, Guangdong, China

evidence.tested: A random-forest model predicted neovascular glaucoma risk in diabetic-retinopathy patients with reported diagnostic metrics. The result is limited to the reported study population and evaluation; the source does not establish transfer to other populations or improved clinical outcomes.
evidence.unknown: The study does not establish improved patient outcomes or generalization beyond the evaluated setting.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
